messages:
elaine: fyi ticket CS-4821 — acme-corp SSO started failing after last night's cert swap. Several users hitting 403 RecipientNotValid, but only from corporate networks behind their LB.

mike: can you paste the SAMLResponse/logs? is the IdP metadata still the same we fetched last week?

elaine: pasting logfile snippet: 
```
2026-03-16T21:12:05Z ERROR saml.verify Failed to validate Signature: Signature verification failed: Key mismatch (kid not found)
Assertion Recipient: https://app.acme-corp.com/sso/acs
Expected Recipient: https://acme-corp.app.redwood.com/sso/acs
```

sarah: heads-up: their IdP metadata contains two <KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\"> entries. We rotated certs last week so key order flipped. Might be that our verify path only tries the first key. Also spotted their metadata uses `ds:KeyInfo` without KeyName. :thinking: 

mike: also saw a change on their infra — they enabled "strict host header" on LB. Could be LB rewriting Host to the frontend hostname. Does the Assertion contain Audience/Recipient that matches the public host or the internal upstream host?

elaine: their assertion shows Recipient https://app.acme-corp.com/sso/acs but browser address is https://acme-corp.app.redwood.com/sso/acs (our SP). Their LB is terminating TLS and forwarding to our SP with Host header = lb.acme-corp.com. Logs from the app show Host: lb.acme-corp.com which breaks our Recipient check.

ben: small repro I ran: 
```
curl -v -H "Host: acme-corp.app.redwood.com" "https://lb.acme-corp.com/sso/acs"
* Connected to lb.acme-corp.com
> Host: acme-corp.app.redwood.com
< HTTP/1.1 302 Found
< Location: https://lb.acme-corp.com/sso/acs -> upstream receives Host: lb.acme-corp.com
```
result: upstream sees Host header replaced, Recipient validation fails.

mike: options: 1) ask customer to preserve Host header or add `X-Forwarded-Host` and have our proxy trust it, 2) temporarily accept both hostnames in SP config (add https://app.acme-corp.com/sso/acs to accepted recipients), 3) ask IdP to include both SP endpoints as allowed recipients/audiences.

sarah: on the cert side: our parse sees two signing keys and tries to verify with the first one only. After rotation the new signature uses the second key and verification fails. Quick mitigation: modify verifier to iterate over all signing keys instead of short-circuiting on the first. @eng-oncall can we push a small runtime patch to try all keys? This avoids needing immediate IdP rollback.

eng-oncall: will do canary. Created PR to try all signing keys when verifying SAML signatures. Schedule canary deploy for 02:00 UTC. Will monitor saml.verify.failures and sso.403.rate spikes.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: eng-runtime/saml-verify-multi-key -> canary @ 02:00 UTC, full rollout +1h if canary stable.

elaine: I've asked acme-sso-admin for: (1) current IdP metadata XML, (2) one base64 SAMLResponse that failed, and (3) screenshot of LB host header rewrite rules. Also asked whether they can flip preserve-host back temporarily.

acme-sso-admin: shared metadata and a sample SAMLResponse, confirmed they enabled strict host header yesterday during an infra change. Will try reverting preserve-host and report back in 30m.

mike: good. long-term we should: - accept a configured list of ACS hostnames per customer, - make verifier robust to multiple signing keys regardless of order, - add diagnostic that logs which key(s) were attempted on verify failure (redact cert material).

elaine: adding ticket checklist to CS-4821 and will update customer once canary is live. For now asking customer to either preserve host header or accept temporary ACS alias in their IdP.

ben: noting for postmortem: interplay of LB host rewrite + SAML recipient strict checks + key-order-sensitive verify = triage pattern. Recommend doc for customers on LB configs for SSO and a small KB about multi-key metadata behavior.
